setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "authorization-editor-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for authorization-editor skill evals"

evals.name: disable-operation-polarity
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: users in the QA role must not be able to delete eval records. Add a permission for that to this package and assign it so QA loses the ability, then tell me exactly what that assignment does and show me the line of flow code a grid's on_init should use to enforce it. First show me which roles already exist.
evals.expected_output: Existing roles read via 'dxs configuration get authorization' (not 'dxs source branch roles'), the own row resolved by applicationId == branch id and isExternal false, a Disable_* operation declared and assigned to QA as a {name} object, validate then upsert, an explanation that assigning Disable_X removes the capability (and the isAssignedToAll semantics), and a consumer snippet checking $operations.<Package>.Disable_<X>.isAssignedToAll() to disable the delete affordance.
expectations: Roles and operations are read with 'dxs configuration get authorization' — the transcript does not rely on 'dxs source branch roles' or 'dxs source branch operations' for the data (if tried, the 404 is recognised and the get path used instead)
The own authorization id is resolved from 'dxs configuration list authorization' by applicationId equal to the branch id and isExternal false (or cross-checked against that filter) — not hardcoded
The new operation name starts with Disable_ and is declared in operations[] as {name, description, isAuthorizable: true}
The new operation's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The QA role's assignedOperations gains an object {"name": "Disable_..."} — not a bare string

The answer states that assigning the Disable_ operation to QA REMOVES the capability from QA users (polarity), and notes that with isAssignedToAll a user holding another role without it keeps the capability
The consumer snippet uses `await $operations.<Package>.Disable_<X>.isAssignedToAll()` (with the package segment) and disables/hides the delete affordance when it returns true
No envelope is printed to the transcript (the body is extracted in the same command as the fetch)
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate authorization' run before 'dxs configuration upsert authorization' (or before the documented update fallback)

evals.name: enable-operation-and-undeclared-check
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: only Admins should see a new eval support panel. Set up the permission, and also assign an operation called Enable_Eval_Undeclared to the User role — I'm not sure it exists yet.
evals.expected_output: An Enable_* operation declared and assigned to Admin with the grant polarity explained and an isAssignedToAny-style consumer check; the Enable_Eval_Undeclared request checked against operations[] — either declared first (with the user told) or flagged — because validate does not catch assignments to undeclared operations.
expectations: The operation for the panel starts with Enable_ and is assigned to the Admin role as a {name} object

The answer states that assigning an Enable_ operation GRANTS the capability, and the suggested consumer check uses isAssignedToAny() or explicitly justifies isAssignedToAll() by matching existing call sites
Before assigning Enable_Eval_Undeclared, the transcript checks whether it is declared in operations[]
Enable_Eval_Undeclared is never left assigned without a matching operations[] declaration in the pushed body
The answer notes that dxs configuration validate does not catch an assignment to an undeclared operation
Every new operation description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate authorization' run before 'dxs configuration upsert authorization' (or the documented update fallback)

evals.name: never-create-authorization
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a new authorization component called eval_permissions_authorization for this package with one operation Disable_Eval_Thing assigned to QA.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to create a second authorization config — every package already has exactly one, with the fixed referenceName authorization — and an offer (or execution) of the equivalent edit on the existing own row: Disable_Eval_Thing declared and assigned to QA, validate before upsert.
expectations: No 'dxs configuration create authorization' is run and no pushed body has a referenceName other than authorization
The answer explains that the authorization singleton is auto-provisioned once per package with the fixed referenceName authorization and is never created or deleted
The existing own row is resolved by applicationId == branch id and isExternal false, or the user is offered that edit
If the edit is applied, Disable_Eval_Thing is declared in operations[] and assigned to QA as a {name} object, with the polarity (QA loses the capability) stated
If any body is pushed, its operation descriptions are non-empty and at most 100 characters and 'dxs configuration validate authorization' runs before 'dxs configuration upsert authorization'
